label: text
text: PRESUMABLY FOUNDERED.

label: text
text:
VERDIOT ON LOCAL COASTING
MYSTER

label: text
text: Reference to the necessity of wireless on digital steamers was made by Mr. G. K. Hall Brutton representing the China Coast Officers' and Marine Engineers of China Guilds, and the relatives of deceased officers) at the Court of Inquiry which sat this morning to investigate the circumstances attending the disappearance of the local steamer "Yue Ying Wa" from the high seas.

label: text
text: In its finding the Court expressed the opinion that the ship, unclassed, had left Hoihow on August 8 for Hongkong, with a general cargo of about 300 tons including livestock, had failed to arrive and had presumably foundered at sea, in a typhoon, with all hands. Further, the Court found that the vessel had not been fitted with wireless; had she been so fitted, her fate would have been known with more certainty.

label: text
text: The Court comprised:—Lieut.-Comdr. G. F. Hole, R.N., Harbour Master (President), Lieut.-Comdr. H. M. C. Purden, O.B.E., R.N., (H.M.S. "Ambrose"). Mr. W. J. Donohue (master of the s.s. "Bowes Castle"), Mr. C. Shearer (master of the s.s. "Harvard") and Mr. A. M. Frame (master of the "Changsha").

label: text
text: When Mr. Brutton addressed the President with a view to the Court incorporating in its verdict remarks on the necessity of wireless installation on ships, he emphasised the strong recommendations by the Court which at in Shanghai to inquire into the loss of the s.s. "Mylie" in 1923. Lieut.-Com. Hole replied that Mr. Brutton, was entering "controversial subjects" but promised to do what was within the scope of the Court.

label: text
text: Mr. F. G. Vaux appeared for the owners, the Cheong Yue S.S. Co., and he asked the President to add in the finding that the ship was lost with all hands.

label: text
text: Evidence was given by Captain G. D. M. Arthur, marine superintendent for the company. After the ship had been five days out—and the voyage only took 30 hours—the owners were advised by letter of the "Yue Ying Wa's" departure. A search, as reported at the time, was mentioned by Captain Arthur.

label: text
text: Other points in his evidence was that the "Yue Ying Wa" was supposed to have gone through the Hainan Straits. six hours ahead of the French s.s. "Limchow" and that the typhoon passed to the back of the latter vessel. Therefore, the French boat experienced heavier weather than the "Yue Ying Wa."

label: text
text: Captain Arthur also said that the ship was not at all overloaded and that the life-saving apparatus was well in order.

label: text
text: The life-raft cylinders (painted grey) sighted by the "Limchow" were similar to those on the lost steamer.

label: text
text: Mr. W. R. Hillyer, Boarding Officer, gave evidence as to official records of the ship's clearance from Hoihow and as to not having since seen her in Hongkong.

label: paragraph_title
text: FEWER TOURISTS.

label: text
text: LOCAL SILK STORE LOSE TRADE

label: text
text: EFFECTS OF THE STRIKE

label: text
text: SHAMEEN STOCKS BROUGHT TO HONGKONG

label: text
text: PRICE, $3.00 Per Month.

label: text
text: Looking at their glittering windows and splendid wares, most people think that the local Indian stores are among the Colony's few thriving concerns.

label: text
text: Yet the local Indian merchants were also badly hit by the strike and the position which it created. However a gradual improvement is now taking place.

label: text
text: The silk stores have suffered heavy losses owing to the Canton market—the source of their supplies—being closed, and the coast ports discontinuing purchases of Indian goods.

label: text
text: The branches at Shameen are all closed, and to prevent deterioration stocks of valuable material have been removed to Hongkong.

label: text
text: Orders from foreign places for Chinese silks, shawls and other goods are for the major part held up. In the earlier months of the strike Canton goods were unobtainable, but the position has improved by small supplies coming via Shanghai, which involves delay and higher cost.

label: text
text: The trade with local customers also suffered for economic reasons. In normal times tourists visiting at odd intervals other than the excursion season increased the turnover of the silk shops, but the number visiting the Colony during the strike has been small and business has naturally suffered.

label: text
text: The imports consist largely of shellac, gunny bags and Indian produce. The business is done on an indent basis, and with the tightness of money and the closing of the Canton market, which received a large share of the purchases of the local Chinese customers; trade came to a standstill during July and August. A little business, however, is now being done in gunny bags, the larger part of which is re-shipped to Shanghai.

label: text
text: With an improvement taking place gradually, the silk stores are making reduced profits and are on the whole not so badly affected as other trades.

label: text
text: Cassia, which forms an important article of export to India, comes from Canton, and since June not a single bag has been shipped, although the merchants have large orders on hand. The trade in Chinese produce is also at a standstill.

label: text

label: text
text:
Pittsburgh, October 15.
Over 40,000 rain-soaked, delirious enthusiasts cheered to victory, the home players who by prodigious labour had overcome an initial lead of four runs scored by Washington in the first innings.

label: text
text: (Reuter's American Service.)

label: text
text: With a. change pitcher, the Pirates drew up to tie the score only to be again left behind by the Senators.

label: text
text: Finally in the eighth inning when the score was again tied and bases full, one of the Pittsburgh out-fielders at the bat, smashed a two-bagger. This mighty fly definitely turned the tide of the battle.

label: text
text: . OFFICIAL STATEMENT

label: text
text:
A British communiqué states that the Conference, after adopting the text of the draft of the Security Pact took up the question of Arbitration Treaties and invited representatives of Poland and Czechoslovakia to join in a meeting to hear statements in regard to the work of the jurists on the Draft Treaties on arbitration between Germany and France on the one part, and Germany and Belgium on the other, the texts of which have been adopted by the Delegations concerned.
The representatives of Poland and Czechoslovakia then gave the Conference an account of their own negotiations with the representatives of the German Government in regard to drafting the Arbitration Treaties between Germany and Poland on the one part, and Germany and Czechoslovakia on the other.

label: paragraph_title
text: NOT BO SURE?

label: text
text: It is semi-officially stated in Government circles in regard to the result of the Conference, that it is extremely satisfactory for all the Powers concerned, but in Berlin there is a guarded tone apparent in Press command over the adoption of the Draft Security Pact, pending a solution of such questions as its effect on the Rhineland occupation, the Saar regime, and other unarranged matters.

label: text

PLAYED FOR IRELAND IN
DAYIS CUP

label: text
text: The wedding took place quietly at the Cathedral this morning of Dr. Richard Edward Tottenham, University of Hongkong, and Miss Norah Margaret Daly, who had just arrived in the Colony from Ireland.

label: text
text: The wedding was to have taken place yesterday, but had to be hurriedly re-arranged on account of the delay of the s.s. "Mantua" which did not arrive until yesterday evening.

label: text
text: The ceremony was without music and was attended by a few personal friends only.

label: text
text: Dr. Tottenham is best known to the Hongkong public on account of his prowess at tennis. He has represented Ireland in Davis Cup matches and shortly after his arrival in Hongkong this year he took part in the exhibition matches in Hongkong against the American star players who visited Hongkong, also in exhibition games at the Chinese Recreation Club.

label: text
text: Dr. Tottenham's interest in tennis is not likely to suffer in the least as a result of this happy event; it is understood that the bride is a player of no mean ability.

label: paragraph_title
text: MEFFAN—MUIRHEAD

label: text
text:
A pretty wedding also took place to-day at Union Church; Hongkong, the parties being Miss Helen D. Muirhead, eldest daughter of Mr. and Mrs. William Muirhead, of Bannockburn, Scotland, and Mr. Norman D. Meffan, of Tarkham Dock, eldest son of the late Mr. and Mrs. Richard L. Arbroach, Scotland.
The bride was given away by Mr. R. Wallace and was prettily attired in a simple tunic dress of ivory silk georgette with pearl and diamante trimming, veil of white, embroidered net with wreath of orange blossoms and white heather. Her bouquet was of white roses and Honolulu creeper.

label: text
text: Miss Nancy McNeillie, the bridesmaid, wore a dress of coral pink embroidered georgette with soft blue French crinoline hat and carried a bouquet of pink roses and Honolulu creeper.

label: text
text: The matron of honour, Mrs. D. McNeillie, was attired in grey crepade chine with condor hat of black hatters plush.

label: text
text: The best man was Mr. W. Robertson.

label: text
text: Mr. S., Collett, at the organ, played suitable music and during the service the hymns: "The Voice that breathed o'er Eden" and "O God of Bethel" were sung.

label: text
text: A reception at the Hongkong Hotel grill room followed the service and Mr. and Mrs. Meffan then left for Repulse Bay where the honeymoon is being spent. The bride's going away dress was of fawn. georgette with overdress of fuschiu. flowered chiffon and hat to match.
